best_for: Writers, students and researchers who want their notes as plain Markdown files on their own disk, and who may later pay for Sync instead of wiring up their own.

points.title: Free, no sign-up
points.text: The app is free with no feature limits and needs no account. A commercial license costs USD 50 per user per year, and Obsidian says it is not required for work use; it is a way for companies to support the app.

points.title: Your notes are files you own
points.text: Notes live in a folder on your device as plain Markdown, so any editor can open them and they work offline. Obsidian says it cannot read them.

points.title: Sync is the paid add-on
points.text: Sync Standard is USD 4 a month billed yearly or 5 monthly: 1 vault, 1 GB, 5 MB files, 1 month of history. Sync Plus is 8 or 10: 10 vaults, 10 GB (up to 100 GB), 200 MB files, 12 months of history. Both encrypt end to end. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Publishing costs extra
points.text: Obsidian Publish, which turns notes into a website, is USD 8 per site a month billed yearly or 10 monthly.

points.title: Not open source
points.text: The app is closed source under Obsidian's own license, which Flathub flags as non-free. The Flatpak is still marked verified as published by Obsidian, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Plugins and Canvas
points.text: Thousands of community plugins and themes extend it, and Canvas gives you an endless board for laying out notes, images and links.

points.title: Installers and history
points.text: Windows gets per-user or all-users installers for x64, 32-bit and Arm64. The Mac app is a universal .dmg that needs macOS 12 or later. The Windows listing keeps 71 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
